title: Working from Home – Can Experiences from the COVID-19 Pandemic Help Facilitate the Extensive Energy Modernization of the University Building?
content: The study aims to analyze the possibility of periodically introducing work from home during the energy modernization of the university building. A detailed modernization concept was devel-oped in 2017 as part of the KOD-nZEB project. As a result of the modernization, the primary energy consumption in the building is to decrease from approx. 150 to 6.2 kW/m2, to the standard of nearly zero energy building nZEB. A significant obstacle affecting the implementation plan is the need to maintain the uninterrupted operation of the faculty. Based on the experiences gained during the COVID-19 pandemic, the hybrid mode of work-from-home (WFH) concept was suggested to fa-cilitate modernization. A survey was conducted among academic staff to verify this assumption. The measurement procedure for assessing the environment in workplaces organized in homes and at the university was developed. Additionally, a different form of supporting the faculty staff in organizing home workplaces is foreseen. People who do not have the local conditions for providing WFH or who have classes could temporarily use workplaces organized in the faculty building could temporarily use "hot desks." The analyses showed that it is possible to reduce the time spent by academic staff in the building by approximately 65%.
